subtopic: VPC CIDR Subnetting (Public vs Private vs Isolated Subnets)
question_text: [Cloud Infrastructure & Virtual Networks (VPC, Subnets) - Q06] What routing configuration distinguishes a public subnet from a private subnet in an AWS Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)?

options.text: A public subnet has an explicit route in its route table pointing `0.0.0.0/0` to an Internet Gateway (IGW); a private subnet routes `0.0.0.0/0` to a NAT Gateway or has no internet egress
Public subnets have 10.0.0.0/8 IP ranges; private subnets have 192.168.0.0/16 ranges
Private subnets disable all security groups
Public subnets do not support EC2 instances

answer_explanation: The definition of a public subnet in cloud networking is having a route table destination `0.0.0.0/0` targeting an Internet Gateway, allowing public IPv4 allocation and direct inbound internet routing.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: The definition of a public subnet in cloud networking is having a route table destination `0.0.0.0/0` targeting an Internet Gateway, allowing public IPv4 allocation and direct inbound internet routing.
